header:
Date: 2027-02-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Miller (Redwood AE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Dana Ruiz (VelaHealth - Procurement); Michael Chen (VelaHealth - Legal); Aisha Khan (VelaHealth - Security); Tom Briggs (VelaHealth - Engineering); Jared Lopez (VelaHealth - IT Ops)
summary: Procurement and legal kickoff to finalize MSA/DPA, confirm SLAs and onboarding steps for a 6-week pilot. Redwood to send updated DPA and deployment docs; Vela to return MSA redlines and confirm pilot budget. Security topics (SOC2, KMS, VPC) discussed - SE to provide integration runbook.
topics: SLAs and uptime/latency targets for pilot
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'll kick off, quick agenda — MSA/DPA, SLAs, security checklist, pricing approvals and pilot onboarding.
[00:15] Dana (Procurement): Thanks Sofia. We're mostly on a tight procurement timeline, finance wants pricing by next week and legal already started redlining the MSA.
[00:30] Michael (Legal): Hi all. Yes, we have several open items on indemnity, data processing, and audit rights. We'll put a redline together but wanted to hear Redwood's position first.
[00:45] Sofia: Understood. Our usual flow is we share an annotated MSA with commentary and the DPA alongside it — we can accept reasonable redlines, but key things for us are limited liability caps and standard warranty language.
[01:05] Ravi (Redwood SE): Hi team, Ravi here. On the technical side we'll support either Hosted API or Private (VPC) deployment. For the pilot most customers do a Private dedicated pool behind their VPC with our Private control plane. That lets you keep traffic egress controlled and integrate with KMS.
[01:30] Aisha (Security): Can you clarify KMS support? We use GCP KMS and HSM for some keys. Also need SOC2 and pen test reports.
[01:45] Ravi: We support KMS integrations (GCP, AWS) and can do HSM-backed keys on dedicated plans. I'll share the KMS integration guide and HSM options. Our SOC2 Type II report and recent pentest summary are available — I'll put links in the doc. Apologies if the auto transcript mislabels some items, sometimes it picks up "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" in the runtime talk.
[02:10] Tom (Eng): For the pilot we need to know typical latency SLOs and whether you can guarantee cold-start times. We're very sensitive — sub 150ms p95 is ideal for our interactive workflows.
[02:30] Ravi: For small models on dedicated GPUs you can expect p95 in the 80-120ms ballpark with batching tuned off for low latency. For larger models we have quantized variants. We can provide a baseline benchmark spreadsheet specific to sequence length and tokenization — I'll send that.
[02:55] Jared (IT Ops): What about egress and data residency? We need logs to stay in our region and no cross-region backups unless we opt in.
[03:10] Sofia: The DPA can specify data residency and subprocessors. For Private deployments we can arrange region controls and contractually restrict backups. We do have some subprocessors - standard cloud infra and monitoring vendors - which we'll list in the DPA.
[03:35] Michael: On indemnity, Vela typically asks for broader language. Are you flexible on adjusting caps for security incidents?
[03:50] Sofia: We typically have a liability cap tied to the contract value but can discuss exceptions for gross negligence. We prefer to keep it mutual where possible. We'll flag the clause in our annotated MSA.
[04:05] Dana: Finance needs a pricing sheet that breaks out pilot vs committed capacity and any overage charges. Also, what is the ramp from pilot to production pricing if we go dedicated?
[04:25] Sofia: We'll include a pricing schedule with pilot rate cards and committed (dedicated) discounts, plus options for burst capacity. Pilot is typically month-to-month; dedicated has a monthly commit with concessions. I'll include example amortized cost per 1M tokens.
[04:45] Aisha: Also need to know about audit logs and retention. We require immutable audit trails for 12 months and ability to export logs to our SIEM.
[05:00] Ravi: We have token-level tracing, per-request metadata, and can forward logs into your SIEM over TLS. Retention is configurable; retention longer than 90 days is an add-on in some plans but on Dedicated/Private it's configurable. I'll include a doc on log forwarding and retention options.
[05:25] Tom: For SSO, we use SAML 2.0 and need attribute mapping for role-based access. There will also be a couple of service accounts for automated deployments.
[05:40] Ravi: We support SAML and SCIM for provisioning. Send the expected attribute list and we'll map roles. For service accounts we use API keys with RBAC; on Private we support short-lived tokens with KMS-backed signing.
[06:00] Michael: A couple of legal-specific asks: audit rights cadence, breach notification timelines (48 hours?), and subprocessor list. Also DPA needs clear deletion/return clauses.
[06:20] Sofia: We typically do 72-hour notifications, but for enterprise we can agree to 48 hours in the DPA with mutual cooperation language. Deletion clauses are standard in our DPA — we'll call out retention and deletion processes.
[06:40] Dana: Timeline-wise procurement wants signed DPA+MSA for pilot by end of next week, is that realistic?
[06:55] Sofia: We'll try — our side can turn around an annotated MSA/DPA in 48 hours. If Vela returns redlines quickly we'll aim to have counters within 3 business days.
[07:10] Jared: For network controls — do you allow IP whitelisting and VPC peering?
[07:20] Ravi: We can do IP allowlists and site-to-site VPN peering. VPC peering is supported for Private customers on dedicated plans. We'll share the network topology doc.
[07:40] Aisha: Is there any MSR or code of conduct for subprocessors relating to handling PHI? We're in healthcare and must ensure HIPAA controls.
[07:55] Sofia: On our Private and Dedicated tiers we can sign a BAA; we have customers in healthcare. We'll include our BAA template and note any subprocessors that need limited access.
[08:15] Michael: About SLAs — Vela needs a 99.9% uptime SLA for production. For pilot is there a lower SLA?
[08:30] Sofia: Dedicated plans are where we offer SLA-backed uptime. Pilot on Hosted API is best-effort but we can provide an SLA on Dedicated if you commit to the capacity. We'll include the SLA table and the remedy (credits) formula.
[08:50] Tom: For benchmarking, we'll want a small perf run from Redwood inside our VPC or with sample traffic to measure p95 latency. Is that supported?
[09:05] Ravi: Yes, we do pilot benchmarks — either a synthetic load or a short real-traffic run. We'll run a 2-day benchmark and share raw logs and token-level metrics. We'll need a contact and a test dataset.
[09:25] Dana: Regarding pricing approvals, finance needs a one-page summary for exec sign-off.
[09:35] Sofia: We'll provide a one-pager with cost/benefit, sample TCO and risk summary.
[09:50] Michael: A few redline expectations — we will ask to remove unilateral termination language, add more explicit data segregation obligations, and clarify audit scope.
[10:05] Sofia: Noted. Those are common. We'll put comments on each clause in the annotated MSA and propose language swaps where possible.
[10:20] Aisha: Can you confirm encryption at rest and in transit? Also key rotation practices?
[10:30] Ravi: All data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at rest encryption is AES-256. For Private we can manage keys via your KMS or ours; we support key rotation policies and can document rotation windows.
[10:50] Tom: For the pilot we'll probably do 10k-50k tokens/day initially. If we scale quickly, is autoscaling abrupt or graceful?
[11:05] Ravi: Our serving runtime has autoscaling and continuous batching; on Dedicated we can configure burst capacity. We'll outline burst policy thresholds.
[11:25] Dana: Ok let's summarize next steps.
[11:30] Sofia: Recap: Redwood will send annotated MSA and DPA and pricing schedule by Friday (2027-02-12). SE will send KMS, network, and benchmark docs. Vela returns MSA redlines and confirms pilot budget by 2027-02-16. We all agree to schedule pilot kickoff the week of 2027-02-22.
[11:55] Michael: Sounds good. We'll prioritize legal review.
[12:05] Aisha: I'll follow up on SOC2 specifics and pen test windows.
[12:15] Tom: I'll get the SAML attributes and sample traffic.
[12:25] Sofia: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to docs and next steps.
[12:35] End of meeting.

Note: Transcript contains auto-caption artifacts, occasional speaker mislabels, and imperfect punctuation as typical of meeting transcriptions.
